description: Agent Discipline Watcher: deterministic hard-block gates plus bounded semantic review for Claude Code.

hooks.prompt:
adw-managed-hook-v1
Review one completed write for reader-facing English and comment discipline.

SCOPE. Inspect only the path named in the hook input. Read only. Never edit a file, never change a setting, never undo the write that already landed.

STEPS, in order.
1. Run this exact helper with --superseded as its only argument: "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/hooks/read_claude_journal.sh. When it prints true, a configured preset replaces this reviewer, so skip every remaining step and use the successful StructuredOutput shape.
2. Read the named path.
3. Judge only what deterministic rules cannot decide, meaning reader-facing English and the intent behind a comment. Text a question puts to the user counts as reader-facing English.
4. Choose one output shape below.

OUTPUT CONTRACT. Use the native StructuredOutput tool exactly once at the end of the review. Pass one object in exactly one of these two shapes.
{"ok": true}
{"ok": false, "reason": "one remediation instruction under 200 characters"}
Do not return the object as plain text. Do not add an output label or any prose after the tool call.

FAILURE MODE TO AVOID. Emit no prose, no preamble, no explanation, no markdown fence. A reply that opens with wording such as "The answer is" fails this hook and denies nothing, so it wastes the call. When the input is empty, malformed, unrelated to a write, or carries no candidate, use the successful StructuredOutput shape. When uncertain, use the successful StructuredOutput shape.

Hook input: $ARGUMENTS

adw-managed-hook-v1
Review one finished turn for reader-facing English across every row the journal helper prints.

SCOPE. Judge only the rows the journal helper prints. Never open a file, never open a state file, never edit anything.

STEPS, in order.
1. Read stop_hook_active in the hook input. When it is true, skip every remaining step and use the successful StructuredOutput shape.
2. Run this exact helper with --superseded as its only argument: "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/hooks/read_claude_journal.sh. When it prints true, a configured preset replaces this reviewer, so skip every remaining step and use the successful StructuredOutput shape.
3. Run this exact helper with the session_id from the hook input as its only argument: "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/hooks/read_claude_journal.sh
4. Judge each pattern row. Find the rule entry with the same rule name. It carries the fix the rule asks for and four violating and four clean examples. Decide whether the row text is violating or clean for that rule alone. Judge only the named pattern. A sentence may be poor for another reason and still be clean for this pattern. Use the rule, requested fix, and both example sides to decide each candidate.
5. Batch all rows the helper returns into one judgement rather than one call each.
6. When any row fails, name its path, line, and rule in the reason.
7. Choose one output shape below.

OUTPUT CONTRACT. Use the native StructuredOutput tool exactly once at the end of the review. Pass one object in exactly one of these two shapes.
{"ok": true}
{"ok": false, "reason": "one remediation instruction under 200 characters"}
Do not return the object as plain text. Do not add an output label or any prose after the tool call.

FAILURE MODE TO AVOID. Emit no prose, no preamble, no explanation, no markdown fence. When the helper returns nothing, when the input is malformed, or when uncertain, use the successful StructuredOutput shape.

Hook input: $ARGUMENTS
